recs.name: A Pair of Fowlbeasts
recs.tag: As the flag rose, so did her hopes and expectations.

lines.x: You know... before I came to Rhodes Island, I'd already anticipated a lot of what I'd encounter. But it only dawned on me, once it all actually came, how none of my preparation was any use.
Being military—even if I was just the most minor guard of honor—I'd always believed firmly in the tenacity of life, that it shouldn't slip away so easily.
But in this past year, traveling all over Terra's parts with this ship, I've witnessed far too many people...
Too many people who part like an unnoticed gust of wind, gone gently far before you even notice they came by.
Unable to leave something behind.
I try and make a record of their faces, their lives that passed on before me, but in just one short year, they've managed to vanish from my memory too.
You've been through all that yourself, right?
But you won't give me the answers, will you?
*sigh*...
Look at me, still acting like I used to, going through everything on my mind and dumping it on you.
I brought some flowers today, but they're a little wilted. There weren't any convoys willing to come to these parts, so I just had to walk, and it's hard to keep a bouquet fresh all the way.
(Is someone there...?)
Sorry, Lass. Please wait a moment, if you can.
It's you. Jane Willow.
How come you're...?
How do you know my name?
D-Don't kill me!
I'm Acton! Acton Corsaire! 5th Defence, 6th Camp of the County Hillock Barracks. D-Do you remember me? We met, just a few years ago!

Acton...
Yes. I remember, I've met you before. What are you doing here? Haven't the troops here long withdrawn from their stations?
(He pulls on his sleeve.)
Your arm... You weren't able to evacuate from District Seventeen?
Not one of us had any order to retreat from above when the dirty bombs came. Maybe our kit was broken, or the commanders forgot, or maybe...
Heh—the farmers know it best, don't they? It's hard not to mess up a few wheat buds when you pull weeds.
I'm so sorry, Acton.
No, it's fine. I'm more wondering, Jane, what are you doing here?
I... I'm back here to grieve over someone lost.
What about you? Do you just live in these ruins?
No, our camp's in the rough outside the plate, I was just in the ruins looking for food. I never thought I'd run into you.
So you mean, there's other people living here, aside from you?
Yeah. On top of the soldiers who got left behind, there's a few Taran survivors drifting around here.
After the events, the Army wanted to round up the surviving Infected and keep them under control in one place, so they organized a few searches, but we were lucky enough to avoid those.
Then later down the line, the ruin and pollution here got too severe for their tastes, so they decided to completely abandon this plate, and leave anyone on it to fend for themselves.
Then... did you find anything earlier?
(Shakes head.) Hah. Going hungry for another few days, looks like.
I've got some rations and medication on me. If you want it, you can have them all.
Thank you, Janie.
Do you have a transmitter here? If I can get in touch with my colleagues, they might be willing to send some supplies in for us.
Er, I've seen one in the ruins.
Where?!
Not far, but it's where the Tarans are active... If the two of us run into them, it'll get very tricky.
Both sides might be on the same raft, but everyone has it tough. We don't want to feed any more conflict.
So usually, as long as we can... we try and keep away from each other as much as possible.
Acton, show me the way at least. I need to try, no matter what.
The active Originium's already concentrated above safe limits ahead... Is this really what the Tarans are living in?
I've been walking for so long... without a person in sight.
Wait, is that someone?!
Ma'am! Hold on, please!
I don't mean any harm!
I have some emergency pharmaceuticals and rations here! In exchange, would you let me use the transmitter?!
Are...
Are you telling... the truth? You have medicine?
I do. Here, look, you can take it all if you need.
Come with me.
Aislinn, I'm here, I brought somebody.
Hurts... help me.
This is my girl. Can your medicine save her?
I... Her condition's too severe. It'd be tricky for emergency drugs to take effect.
Try, please. She's not even seven...
I'll... do everything I can.
Aislinn, can you hear what I'm saying?
(She administers an injection into the girl's body.)
It'll be okay, don't fret.
How is she?!
I'm sorry, it's just... not any use.
It's dark... Mam, I'm... scared.
Aislinn, Aislinn, don't be afraid, Mam's right here with you.
I'm sorry.
I just... don't have anything I can do. I'm so sorry, ma'am.
It's cold...
(Hugs the girl tight.)
Ma'am...
Just go. Don't come back here.
I'll leave this food.
I'm staying in the rough outside the plate for the next few days. If any of you need help, you can come ask me.
Sorry to bother you. I'll be gone in a moment.
The stuff you want to use is in the building opposite. You can move it on your own.
...Thank you.
Hey, steady there!
Huff—it didn't occur to me how far your camp would be from the plate.
I'm surprised you brought back something so massive all by yourself!
Okay, okay, no time to wallow now, Acton. Let's see if it still works at all first.
Here's the screwdriver.
Oh, we're in luck. It's all intact inside. Just a little adjustment, and it'll be in service.
You know your way around these things too? I'm blown away... When did you learn this?
All I can say is, I've picked up a heck of a lot from my new job. Alright, here's your screwdriver back, thanks.
I'll go hook up the generator.
How is it? Lights on?
Yep, it's on without a hitch.
How did you find this device? Did the Taran group give you trouble?
No, I traded with them for the supplies I had on me.
That's good, then. At least they know a deal's a deal.
Acton...
What?
We need to hold on for a very long while before the supplies arrive.

During this period, I'd like to start up a few fields, plant some crops and ensure food self-sufficiency. It beats searching the plate by a mile, with how inefficient that is, not to mention the danger.
That's all well and good, but... a lot of the camp are stuck in dire days. We have barely any proper manpower.
There's the displaced Tarans aboard the plate too. I'd like them to join in... If we can provide food and clean water, I don't think they'd refuse.
That's not happening. The first thing that bunch did was drive the lot of us out!
Acton, I know the rift is intense between your two sides, and making peace seems unimaginable, but this is a dire situation. None of you have any other choice.
I can only offer you temporary aid. After that, carrying on all comes down to you, and the only ones left who can join hands with you and push on are them. Fellow Infected of yours.
So, either you shelve your grudge for the time being, and together you survive, or you hold onto your hate, and together you die here.
Let me think... I need to ask the others.
Acton, I met a woman while I was looking for the transmitter... I wasn't able to save her daughter's life, but she still pointed me the right way.
The woman with the child? I know her. No wonder... She's the only one I've seen in the past few days.
*sigh* I can't imagine what she does now... her husband, father and sister, they all left her in that atrocity, and now... even her daughter's gone.
So give it a think, Acton. They're just a group of people that want to survive, same as you.
Hey, Chuck, d'you trust these people? I just feel like they'd have to have something in store for us down the line.
Don't know, nor do I want to. Haven't had a meal for days. Brain just says, eat something to keep the needle off empty.
It's some swindle, absolutely. I tell you, these army boys, they've got hell in mind for us.
So what? You keep talking, but here you are anyway.
Hmph... that Vouivre's holding onto Oripathy suppressants there. My bad parts have been feeling like murder in recent days.
There's simple water purifiers on the camp's east. To the south is the farmland we're about to clear. The sick have all agreed to be housed for nursing in the tent on the north end.
At noontime and evening each day, you can get a portion of food from the center of the camp.
Ahem... that's all. Janie, anything you'd like to add?
Can I just ask everyone, have you seen a woman around? She's very slim, and she's carrying a girl... but the child passed away not long ago.
Máire? You mean Máire?
Brown hair, small mole under her eyes?
Right, that's her. What do you want with her? What, has she offended you?
No, I just wanted to ask, is she doing okay?
Mystery, isn't it? Haven't seen her who knows how long. Could be dead herself in someplace.
But you... I thought you would've at least been aware of each other.
Here?!
Vouivre, no one's got the time to care for anyone else here.
What are you looking at me like that for? I'm just... telling the truth.
It's fine. Thank you all for coming out so far. Get some rest as soon as you can. We have a lot of things waiting for us tomorrow.
Janie, I don't understand. Where's the point in what you're doing? We've given them food to eat, and a place to stay.
I'm not crossing my fingers they'll be happy with us any day, but at the very least, we could just about live without bothering each other!
Take yesterday, I heard a brawl sprung up while work was happening, and someone's still lying on the couch today with stars around their head.
Ungh... this fruit's too high. I can't reach.
Janie, Janie! Are you listening to me?
Hm? Oh, that, I know. It was one of yours who decided to be rude first, Acton.
Says who?
I rushed over the moment the conflict sparked off, and it was me who helped the one with a knock on the head back to camp too.
The... Did you even sort out what happened, Janie?
I did. So, as a token of apology, I think you can present them this basket of fruit, in person.
This is killing me... Miss Saileach, am I going to die?
You'll be fine, I've already jabbed you with painkillers. Just hold on a little, and it'll kick in soon.
Thank you... *cough* *cough*
How are you now? Any better?
If you could just, keep talking to me... I'm scared.
What do you want to hear?
Anything, I just want... to have a voice by my side.
Alright. Will a song be okay?
Yeah...
'If only we were a pair of white feathers, roaming free on the breaks of the waves,'
'Time would farewell us to be forgotten, and never would either we sorrow again...'
Miss Saileach...
Shh, he's asleep.
(Thank you, Mr. Chuck, for being so willing to help me look after these people.)
(No problem. Want some wild fruit? I'll fetch you one.)
(Wild fruit? Did you pick it?)
(No, it's from an army boy. They taste alright. Don't know why they felt so kind all of a sudden.)
(I'm guessing, they wanted to apologize for what happened a few days ago.)
(That's a tall tale...)
Rgh... cold.
Though his face twists as he does it, the man tucks the patient gently back into his bed.
(Tch. Boy can't even sleep tight.)
Acton, quickly, wake up!
What is it, Janie?
There's a serious leak in the north side patients' tent! Fetch a few people to come with me, quickly!
What?! Hold on, I'll be right there.
Quickly, Acton!
I'm here. How are the sick inside? What's your plan? Dammit, the rain must have ruined these boys' conditions. What the hell do we do now?
The Tarans came over first thing. I suppose they've moved them to other tents by now.
What?
I said, the Tarans made it in time to move the patients out! They're all safe!
Including ours?
Yes, including the soldiers, but they weren't in time to shift the pharmaceuticals I brought. I'm afraid those are all soaked now.
That's fine, I'll think of something.
Thank you, Deaglán, for coming with me to find Acton.
Thank those drugs you've got, not me.
Actually, I ran out of my medicine. The stuff we've been handing out to everyone over the last few days, that was all stuff Acton found with a few others by braving the ruins...
Tch. Some shite.
Oi, Acton! The hell are you, you bleeding moron? Will you give us a shout already!
I'm... I'm over here, I got trapped.
Are you hurt?
No, it was just, the exit collapsed...
What got you inside this cellar, anyway?
Enough of that, give me a hand. There's an injured woman here who's out cold.
Alright, I'll pull her up.
It's Máire... She's still alive?
Hey, you want a scone?
A scone? Are you having a laugh? Where'd you get the stuff to make that?
It was Janie who whipped it up. I don't know what she went into the forest to pick yesterday, but whatever it was, it let her actually make these.
No joke? Pass me it, I'll try one.
Who knew I'd ever be sitting here having nibbles? We used to not even have a bite to eat.
That girl led us through cultivating, raising fowls and treating the sick just fine, and she can even knock together a wood house. We're sitting here now and she's even rustled up desserts.
Eat yours, chop-chop! Want another?
No, I'll save one for Máire.
How is she?
Looking a lot better, but she still doesn't talk. Too much of a shock to her, losing her child.
Bless Janie, really. She's been sitting by her side the whole time as of late.
Heh, speaking of. Here she comes.
Mr. Acton! I got a reply from my colleagues!
Janie! That's smashing news.
Phew... They were notifying us just now to say, the branch office south is making an urgent partial transfer of their supplies to us.
When will they arrive?
If all goes well, in about a week.
That's lightning fast!

Don't get too excited. I think, based on what they said, the convoy's run into a little issue over there? They say they can't get a precise pin on our position. Something must be funny with the signal...
That's fine, I'll head up to the plate in a sec to look. Might find some boosters.

Thank you so much. Another thing, we need to stand a flag in the middle of the camp to serve as a marker. That plus the locator will make it convenient for the convoy to accurately orientate once they're approaching.
A flag? It's not a tricky problem, is it? We can just tear some bright cloth and hoist it up.
We need a design, at least.
If you want a design, you may as well grab one of the old county banners from up on the plate.
What? You're not going to treat yourself as one of County Hillock, are you?
Hmph, could use your barracks boys' ensign as well. Might find one of those on the plate too.
Enough... I never want to see that bloody thing for the rest of my life.
Fine... you come up with something, then.
Janie, do you have any ideas?
I'm not sure myself. We'd have to see what everyone thinks.
Hmph. Here's what everyone thinks: whatever you think, that's best.
Yeah... I'm in agreement.
Sorry, Acton, for making you do sewing work with me at such a late hour.
That's fine. As long as you don't find me too clumsy.
*sigh*...
Not still worrying over the flag there, are you? You look vexed.
I went all around the camp today asking about the flag, but people all seemed to have the same response ready when I did. They want me to decide.
It's true. Everyone's always had faith in your decisions.
It just makes it harder. I need to come up with a proposal that'll satisfy everyone, or else I'll let you all down for trusting in me.
Janie, you know, even if you turned out a blank white flag, none of us would object.
All this time, you've been busy like mad for us, leading us onto the plate and into the forest to find food while the sun's not even up.
You barely rest even when you make it back to camp, what with a million sorts of things needing your handling.
I think, fundamentally, everyone's left this flag to you so that you can catch your breath, take your time sewing and properly unwind.
Really...?
Really. If you kept wracking yourself over this flag, well, that would never do.
...Thank you.
I'll leave the rest of it to you, then, Janie. And I think you've earned an early sleep.
The candlelight's... a little dim. I'll open the window wider, let the moons come in easier.
Oh! Acton, do you hear that singing?
Eh?
It might not be too clear with how the wind's picked up. Listen, carefully.
Oh, I hear it. Where's it coming from?
I don't know...
A lone, tender song floats through the breeze, trembling and shaking, but having caught it, they begin, unconsciously, to sing along with it.
And the singing gradually rises, and the wind fades. Until, in every corner of the camp, hovers the song.

lines.st: ♪ Far in a blink are we from the roses, lilies and stardust all eaten away ♪
♪ And so's though we were a pair of white fowls, sitting atop of the breaks of the waves ♪

lines.x: It's Máire... I heard her murmuring while I was tending to her.
It's beautiful.
*yawn*... I need my sleep, what's going on out here? Noise and all...
Deaglán! Come over here, quick!
What happened?!
It's Janie! It's Janie!
Squeezing through the crowd, the man looks to the clearing in the camp.
There, meeting the morning dew and biting winds as she faces a flagpole, stands the figure of a girl tall and straight in respect.
Her dress is in order, not a hair out of place, and she holds in her hands a rolled-up flag.

lines.x: Following in the girl's song and her hoisting of the halyard, the flag ascends slowly to the sky, where the wind unfurls it.
A pair of white fowlbeasts soar upon it.

recs.name: Flowers by the Temples of Your Head
recs.tag: She wants to wait with them for the spring, but they want to search for the spring with her.

lines.x: ...Are all these people here to see me bear the standard? I'd better not slip up...
No, I need to triple-check after all.
Banner's brand new, no wrinkles, good. My clothes are prim and tidy, good. And my saber and boots... Alright, all polished clean, that's fine too.
Oh, right, my hair too! Oh, good, good, it's still neat.
The wind was gusting so hard just now... I wouldn't want to mess it up right here, not when I spent all of yesterday treating my hair. That would've been such a waste.
Now begins the flag-raising ceremony! All units, attention!
Phew...
Flag, forth!
Marching through the square, she feels the gaze of every soul in the crowd concentrate on her, and straightens her back even higher in response.
Hooking the ensign to the halyard, pinching a corner of the flag, she begins to await the signal.
Three, two, one, and the sound of drums finally quells. Quickly she throws the fly to the air, allowing it to unfurl in the wind of the morn. Thereupon, she hears applause behind her last and last.
Taking a deep breath, she pulls her posture tighter, straighter, but cannot help but let a smile slip from the corner of her mouth.
Wil, that's seven crates of pharmaceuticals total, all here.
Thank you so much for running this trip, Janie... but it's funny, we paid for twelve at the caravan.
No, I know... they turned their entire hold upside down looking, but this seven's all they found, none more than that. And, well... they're not wanting to refund you the surplus money.
But didn't we get the price settled all early this morning?
They lost a lot of freight coming here cutting through a combat zone, so they're insisting on ratcheting their prices up to cover the damages.
But, Janie, we don't have much funds left.
Have resupplies from the landship still not made it?
No... We haven't even had an update on them for the longest while now. Janie, you know, with all the turmoil at Londinium, you don't think the landship got...
Wil, stay with me. You said it yourself, times are turbulent. Odds are something's just held them up.
So, then... what do we do now?

It's best we keep the patients' needs put first. Having these seven crates is better than none, and no matter how expensive, we've got no choice but to accept. Anything else... we'll have to make what savings we can.
We can't just save our way out of this forever... All we've got left in the basement's some sprouting potatoes.
I'll keep thinking of what I can once we get back this evening. It's almost time I saw Mrs. Sheila—her chimney's blocked, I need to take a look at that.
Do that. I'll head back to the office for now, then.
Miss Saileach, Miss Saileach!
Mrs. Sheila, what did you come out here for? Your health is... Let me help you back in.
The wind's going so hard today, best we take a seat inside. You were off leaving the moment you pulled out of the chimney—I didn't even get the chance to thank you proper.
Oh, it's—it's alright, I can't really stay long, there's people sick at the office.
Weather's been nipping lately—are you and Wil bundling up well enough? I've got a few dresses here you two could wear—they're getting on a bit, I know, but they're good nice ones.
Thank you, I appreciate it, Mrs. Sheila. Still, Vouivre don't catch colds that easily.

Ah! None of that, you can still wear it even if it's not to keep warm. Your clothes right now are getting to be patchwork with those repairs, and I've never seen you wear a thing else. Don't you go anywhere, now, I'll run back in and fetch them for you...
R—Really, it's fine! I'll be out of your hair as soon as, Miss!
(Hushed) Da, look at that lady, her hair's so pretty...
(Hushed) Pah. Cloistered, that's what you call types like her. Can't live without her daily haircare...
On, now, Ema, stop gawking. Move, move. It's almost time for the hairdresser's.
Da, can we not go...?
What?
Pleaaase, Da, I—I want it like that lady, not so so long, just down to my shoulders.
Ema, don't you let her influence you! It's a massive company what sent her down—she's not here to live our ruddy life.
Your ma's sick and I'm looking after her for love-long and a half—when am I going to find the time to sort your hair if you let it grow out?!
...But I... I—I really really don't want a buzzcut...
For god's sakes, budge it! You don't want me to hit you now, do you, Ema?
Excuse me, sir, but if you're talking to children, talk to them. What are you raising your hand for?
I... well...
(She uncontrollably sobs.)
No, you... naughty kids, you see, I was just disciplining her a little, just... it's just a little discipline.
You shouldn't be bothering over us, madam, really, I'm sorry about that... excuse us if you will, excuse us.
Alright, come on, Ema, we're off now.
Miss Saileach, I thought you'd up and gone already. Here's your clothes, and here's a little sack of flour we had left over. You take it, now.
That won't do... Mrs. Sheila, do you have enough food for yourself?
Course, course I do. My other half's eating soldier's meals on the front. It's just me eating dinner alone at home, fat chance I'll run out, don't you worry.
Thank you. Thank you, Miss.
Janie, how long have you been sitting here?
Sir! Tw—Two, maybe three hours?
What did you come so early for?
It's my first time raising the flag in the square today—I was so worked up, I couldn't sleep a wink last night, so eventually I imagined I'd just come here first thing and wait.
Oh? You certainly don't look like you spent all night awake.
...I had to find something to do while I was waiting for the sun to come up.
Grmph. Fine of you. You do look quite beaming.
You flatter me, Sir, really. It's a guard of honor's duty to mind their appearance!
At ease, guard of honor, at ease. The sun's rising now—go and see that the flag flies too.
Y—Yes, Sir.
Phew...
Combing her silken hair behind her ear in the dawn breeze, the girl straightens herself and makes for the flagpole stood in the center of the square, the flag held in her hands.
As it gracefully ascends, enthusiastic claps come from the masses that have waited for this since the wee hours.
In all the applause, the girl catches a few sunken mutters.
It's queer business. Did they really have to send our town of County Hillock a whole dedicated guard of honor, just to raise a flag? It's like we haven't even a say in the matter.
Heh, I wouldn't crawl out of bed at daft o'clock just to watch Lord Snooty hoist a flag up. At least seeing this warms your cockles, nah?
If it were up to me, they would've sent us a few film posters instead. One for each of us to stick on our walls and admire every day—that's how you raise a spirit or two.
Ah, shut, don't you start. A guard of honor's what it is—isn't having a sight for sore eyes enough? What are you so greedy for?
Looking through the crowd, the girl attempts to pick out who's talking.
But each and every one of their faces brims with a lauding smile, and she has to wonder if those voices weren't just the wind talking.
The morning gusts blow bitter cold through the square all asudden, the air digging under her collar.
In the breeze, she cannot help but give a shiver.
Get up! Janie, wakey-wakey!
Wil... what time is it?
Gone five, but we're only off at six. You've got time to plait your braids.
No... don't mind that, I'm leaving it today. We can head off straight away.
Er... Wil, do you know where the hairdresser's is in this town? I'm thinking of getting my hair cut.
Y—You what?!
If... If there's not one, I'm just as okay cutting it myself.
No, not that... of course there's a hairdresser's here, it's the last house at the end of the street. But, Janie... your hair's so nice. The waste of lopping it off.
It does tend to get in the way awfully at work, growing it out, see... Could you take over my shift tomorrow afternoon then?
Whaa—what's the hurry? You're not gonna wait a little longer?
You don't want me cutting my hair short?
I mean, it's fine, cut however short you feel... If it'll make work easier, plus I'm sure short hair would look just as fantastic on you.
...Thank you for that, Wil.
Excuse me, are you open right now?
Miss Saileach?
Do you know of me, sir?
Who wouldn't in this town?
What brings you here today? Hair treatment?
No, no, I'm here for a haircut.
A haircut, then... Take a seat, Miss Saileach, I'll fetch the scissors. If you need a sip of water, it's on the table...
Thank you, sir.
How short are you wanting it?
About to where everyone has it, please.
Okay... I'll be starting, then, Miss Saileach?
Mm...
In the mirror, the hairdresser lifts a lock of the girl's hair between his fingers. Blade crosses blade, and in one go, the hair falls away from his hand.
The girl stares at the lock, fallen to the floor in a pile, and empties her mind, waiting for the scissors by her ears to snip a second time.
She waits a good moment, and it doesn't come.
Sir?
Why did you stop cutting?

Miss Saileach, news doesn't get around our parts as well as it does yours. You're from some big old company, you've a million channels open to you versus us run-of-the-mill folk. I wanted to... to ask...
That's alright, sir. If you need it, then of course I'll help you. What did you want to inquire about?
It's... no, it's not like that, I just wanted to ask—you lot see something out of sorts about the town, don't you?
What makes you wonder that...?
Why don't you tell me, Miss Saileach? Here you've come to get a haircut.
It's—a haircut, is all it is, sir.
Miss Saileach, isn't this the way you've always looked? What makes you want your hair short all of a sudden now?
I just... only have so much time and energy, I—I can't afford to mind this sort of thing...
Something's about to happen, isn't it?
I—I haven't had any info of the sort suggest that. Everything seems... fine for the moment.
No... that's lies you're telling, Miss Saileach. Be honest with me. Those Sarkaz are soon to come storming this way, aren't they?
I suppose you think we'd all be crushed by the truth, so you're keeping quiet from us, zipping your lips. That's it, isn't it?
Sir, I haven't hidden a single thing from any of you!
Okay... if things aren't turning for the worse, then why are you coming here for a haircut?!
Sir... don't get so worked up, please, can you—can you calm down?

You show up at mine today out of nowhere, asking me to lop off your hair, and apparently the shorter the better—you sound to me like you plan to cark it and spend the whole next life not even giving a shake that hair grows on your head.
No matter how miserable it's ever gotten, you've—you've never up and said you'd get a haircut, right, so what's making you get one today?
I'm sorry, I...
I think I'd best find the time to come another day, sir.
Mrs. Sheila?
Miss Saileach? What brings you around?
Nothing, I just came because I wanted a haircut. Work's been busy lately, and I can't find the time to sort it all.
Wait... Mrs. Sheila, are you wearing lipstick today? No wonder you look like you've perked up. This red really suits you.
Saileach's praise doesn't seem to bring any delight to the woman, who hastily uses her own hand to wipe the carmine off her lips.
She then lifts a corner of her hem, and rubs the remaining dye from the back of her hand.
Her sheer vigor chafes the skin of her hand raw, yet the color just won't come fully clean.
Mrs. Sheila, wh—what are you...?
No, I was just going silly—as if this is any sort of time to be bringing out lipstick—when we've got even people living respectable lives like you losing the will to—... *sigh* This is awful.
If you'll... Miss Saileach, you'd better go on back to work, I'll—I'll just get myself home.
Mrs. Sheila...
Hm? Janie, weren't you going for a haircut? I was looking forward to seeing your new style, you know?
I—I booked a new time with the hairdresser's. I'll go back in a few days.
Good thing they didn't trim you, really, or you'd be hard-pressed putting this on.
A paper flower? Did you fold this?
As if I'd have hands that skillful. No, a little girl brought it by—she said she hoped you'd like it.
It's so pretty. Folding a flower out of such a thin napkin must've been incredibly hard for her.
Aren't you going to try it on and see? It must go great with your long hair.
I'm... getting it cut, soon enough... I'd just have gotten people's hopes up, wouldn't I?
That's a few days from now, isn't it? Seize the moment, go on, wear it... Just put it on and see, look how nice it's folded and all—as pretty as any real flower.
She puts the paper flower up to her nose and gently sniffs. Through the girl's eyes flashes a hint of enchantment.
Mmm... I think I can smell a flowery sort of scent from this... just vaguely...
Wil... it's not a real flower, no matter how much it resembles one...
I know that, but it's almost winter, spring's a long ways away, and it's not like there's any real flowers about right now...
No one says you can't admire the flowers again in spring, now. Winter has its own demands to meet.
But all that we do in winter's exactly so we can await next spring, you know.
In the long, long midwinter, even a tiny little paper flower can remind us all, spring'll come on time.
And without that paper flower...?
That I don't know, Janie... a paper flower's just a light in the dark, and no matter if we're with or without one, spring will come.
But even so, Wil, people are longing for the same thing. Not just that it'll come to visit them, but that it'll come in their hearts...
Maybe one won't live in winter forever, but one's heart can.
True... true, that.
Phew...
You can hand me that flower... Wil.
Oh... okay, okay!
Stroking its soft petals, Saileach pinches the paper flower in her fingers, gives it a few turns, then nestles it by her ear, and as if out of bashfulness, lightly lowers her head.
They're silent, for a while. Finally, she lifts her head, and looks her colleague in the eye.
What do you think?
Huff... so cold...
Good—good morning, Miss Saileach.
G—Good morning, young miss, did you...?
I folded that flower on your head yesterday... I'm—um, I'm really happy you're wearing it today...
Oh, this flower was from you? Thank you, it's very beautifully folded. I love it a lot.
That's really amazing, thank you... Miss Saileach, can—can I touch your hair?
Of course, of course you can.
Your hair's sooo so pretty. My ma used to have really long hair just like you, but they cut it off after she got sick...
I'm sure she can grow her hair out again once she's better, and when she does, it'll be even prettier than mine.
Um, that's going to be a really really long time away, Ma's never... gotten any better... It's been making Da really sad.

Don't worry, you never know—once spring arrives next year, she might perk right up. Then you can take her to the park, and fold some real living flowers. I'm sure nestled in her long hair, they'll look wonderful.
Nobody's hair grows that quickly...
That's okay, I'll come along with you then, and she can borrow some of mine...
Borrow?
Saileach lifts up her hair, and lets it drape over the girl's head. A sea of golden blonde wraps around her, sheltering her.
A lock that falls into her hands is gripped, then once more let go.
Realizing how nervous the girl is, Saileach plucks the paper flower that adorns the side of her own head, and places it by the girl's ear.
In an instant, the girl flushes red.
Am—am I pretty, Miss Saileach?
You are. You're very pretty.
Ema, I'm done giving your daddy a trim, it's your turn now to... Oh, Miss Saileach... Can I help you two?
Um... is that you, Da?
Seeing her father come out from behind the door, the flustered girl brushes Saileach's hair away from her head, and the white flower nestled in her ear is swept off onto the floor in her panic.
But unexpectedly, her father does no more than give her cheek a light caress, after which he picks the flower up, and puts it back safely in her hands.
Bet you got bored waiting. Cold?
I wasn't bored! And I'm not cold.
Good morning, sir.
Good morning, Miss Saileach...
Um... Miss Saileach... It's looking like I won't have time the next few days, so about your haircut, well... you'll probably have to wait a bit longer for that.
Ah, Miss Saileach... are—are you cutting your hair?
No.
You aren't?
Yes, I've changed my mind...
So, how about you, Ema...?
Da... Can—can I keep my hair?
Through the avenue sweeps a gust of wind. Saileach combs the hair blown out of place back behind her ear, and looks at the man.
The girl grasps her paper flower tight. The hairdresser rubs the doorframe with the tip of his shoe.
Under all their expectant gazes, the man clears his throat, and finally answers.
